summary: Washington County, OR peak: a 1933 crow's-nest lookout, a 1946 timber tower staffed until 1965 and removed by 1970; no source describes the summit today.

facts.design: Crow's-nest platform in a fir tree with a cabin (1933); wooden L-4 tower with a 14x14 cab (1946); height disputed
facts.status_note: Tower abandoned in 1965 and removed in 1970 per FFLOS; firelookout.com says it is now gone. No source describes the summit today.

staffing.status: Staffed until 1965, the last season; no staffing after that in the sources read

facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry, North West Oregon FPA

events.note: Crow's-nest tree platform with cabin living quarters served as the first lookout (FFLOS); an August 1934 Forest Log item describes a lookout still to be constructed, so the date is contested
Ranger Tom Seth knocked out for a time by lightning, then finished his shift
Oregon lookouts page lists activation on September 9, 1942 for the Portland Filter Center; role not stated
Timber tower with a 14x14 cab replaced the first structures; 35 ft per FFLOS and firelookout.com, 50 ft in a June 1946 Forest Log item about a tower under construction
FFLOS says the tower was abandoned in 1965
FFLOS says removed in 1970; the Oregon lookouts page says Removed with no date

corrections.why: FFLOS and firelookout.com both give 35 ft (about 10.7 m) for the 1946 wooden L-4 tower. The 50-foot (15.2 m) figure comes from a June 1946 Forest Log item about a tower under construction, not the built tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com say 35 ft; a June 1946 Forest Log item quoted by the Oregon lookouts page describes a 50-foot tower under construction. Height is left out of facts; the story reports both.
Wikipedia says the summit had a tower and cabin from 1933 to 1946. FFLOS and the Oregon lookouts page describe a 1946 tower staffed until 1965. The story reports the conflict.
FFLOS dates the crow's-nest lookout to 1933; a 1934 Forest Log item describes a pack trail to a lookout still to be constructed. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: The brief height of 15.2 m matches the 50-foot plan rather than the 35-foot tower; see corrections. No access information was found for the summit (a Komoot summit listing says visitor information is not available), so no access key is set. Agency wording follows the Oregon lookouts page; the brief says Northwest Oregon FPA. Not used: a geocaching page for a different Round Top (4,649 ft, southern Oregon) and an unconfirmed Willhite page. The -2 Round Top record (us-or-round-top-2) is a different site (Jackson County ODF lookout). The stored tower record data/towers/or/us-or-round-top.json still has height_m 15.2; the corrections entry proposes 10.7 (35 ft). That file was not edited in this check.
